findings.claim: Target identity is not drag-session ownership. A plugin drag on target T can end through the host, followed by a user-bind drag on the same still-live T. ownedDrag.lock() will still equal the controller target, so the proposed unload handler ends the user's drag. This counterexample does not require pointer reuse. The proposal needs an ownership mechanism that distinguishes successive drag sessions and invalidates ownership when the host ends the plugin session. Merely retaining a weak target is unsafe to build on.
findings.evidence: "WP<Layout::ITarget> ownedDrag = g_layoutManager->dragController()->target()"; "T && T == ownedDrag.lock()"; "o host encerra drags sozinho a cada tecla/botão"; "um arrastar iniciado por atalho do usuário não é nosso".

findings.claim: The stated no-reentry argument is false: absence of a plugin listener on ended does not mean endDragTarget cannot call plugin code. The supplied dragEnd path dispatches decoration input, and its focus changes can reach the plugin's window.active listener. Running this before removing decorations leaves that callback route present. This proves possible synchronous reentry during unload, not a callback after the library has been unmapped. The latter remains unproved either way. The proposal must account for these callback routes and quiescence ordering rather than certify safety from the ended-listener grep.
findings.evidence: "nenhum ouvinte do plugin existe em ended → nenhum retorno ao módulo"; "Deve rodar antes de remover decorações e timers"; host dragEnd calls "pWindow->presentation().checkInputOnDecorations(INPUT_TYPE_DRAG_END, MOUSECOORDS, DRAGGING_WINDOW)"; that implementation calls "decoration->onInputOnDeco(type, coordinates, data)"; the plugin registers "Event::bus()->m_events.window.active.listen".

findings.where: Sections 2–3, drag state and grouping differences
findings.claim: The inventory omits the new resets of m_draggingTiled at drag begin and end. This state participates in the drag-into-group decision, so the blanket account of grouping as unchanged is incomplete. A changed outcome for a particular sequence is not proved by the excerpts, but a tiled drag followed by a floating drag onto a group is a concrete regression-test candidate. Document this as an investigated state-reset change or a potential observable difference, not as an established BC.
findings.evidence: The DragController diff adds "m_draggingTiled = false" at both begin and end; dragEnd computes "FLOATEDINTOTILED = !pWindow->isFloating() && !m_draggingTiled" and conditions group insertion on "!FLOATEDINTOTILED".

findings.where: Section 2, orphan-release difference and associated tests
findings.claim: The orphan-release account omits the changed definition of a held button. In 0.57 it is tracked per button and pointer, whereas the old code tracks the button alone. A release from pointer B can therefore take the new orphan-release path even while the same button is held on pointer A. This belongs under the already identified release-handling RD; it does not establish a contractual blocker. Add a multi-pointer case if this behavior is in the supported test environment.
findings.evidence: Old code uses "m_currentlyHeldButtons.push_back(e.button)" and compares "other == e.button"; new code uses "m_currentlyHeldButtons.emplace_back(e.button, mouse)" and compares "held.button == e.button && held.pointer.lock() == mouse" before calling "Keybinds::mgr()->onMouseEvent(e, mouse)" for an unmatched release.

findings.where: Probe K, BeginWithDefaults and Actions assertions
findings.claim: The probe is non-vacuous, but several descriptions exceed what their assertions establish. BeginWithDefaults proves that a two-argument call is well-formed, not that the omitted values are nullopt and false. The m_passPressed assertion proves the member's type, not that Actions::mouse reads it. The Actions checks establish return types for the supplied explicit-argument expressions, not exact formal parameter types or the availability of every abbreviated call proposed in the matrix. The supplied header and mouse body independently support the default-value and state-read claims; the mutation results do not turn these into compile-time semantic tests.
findings.evidence: "requires(CLayoutManager& m, SP<Layout::ITarget> t) { m.beginDragTarget(t, MBIND_MOVE); }"; "static_assert(std::is_same_v<decltype(A::state()->m_passPressed), int>, \"Actions::mouse reads this global bind state\")"; the floatWindow assertion supplies "std::optional<PHLWINDOW>{}", while K4 proposes "Config::Actions::floatWindow(TOGGLE_ACTION_ENABLE)".

findings.claim: The claimed error-behavior transition conflates missing dispatcher names with errors returned by existing dispatchers. Existing legacy dispatchers already wrap ActionResult errors into SDispatchResult errors, and dispatchIfKnown discards that result. Direct typed calls eliminate the missing-name lookup; ignoring their results does not itself introduce new error handling. Also, exec's replacement returns optional<uint64_t>, not ActionResult. State the result-discarding/logging policy separately for Actions and spawn.
findings.evidence: K13 says "Falha vira ActionResult com erro em vez de no-op silencioso"; the old wrapper returns "{.success = false, .error = res.error().message}"; dispatchIfKnown invokes "g_pKeybindManager->m_dispatchers[name](arg)" without inspecting the result; K12 specifies "optional<uint64_t>".

findings.where: Contract review statement and section 6, no-BC conclusion
findings.claim: The supplied evidence supports 'no BC identified in the requirements reviewed,' not a completed review of every named contractual source. docs/CONFIGURAVEL.md is part of the owner's contractual set but is absent from the list of consulted documents. Record its review or qualify the coverage. This omission is not evidence that a BC actually exists.
findings.evidence: The classification names "OpenSpec, docs/API.md, docs/CONFIGURAVEL.md", but "Contrato escrito consultado" lists only "openspec/specs/{title-bar,window-snapping,snap-assist,workspace-modes}, docs/API.md".

notes:
The rejection concerns the unsafe Q4 proposal and its incorrect reentry justification, not unauthorized implementation: the material consistently states that nothing was integrated. No demonstrated violation of the owner's enumerated written functional requirements follows from the supplied migration evidence. The major ownership issue is classified RD because the quoted non-interference rule is in QUIESCENCE.md rather than the owner's enumerated functional contract; its classification does not make the proposed cleanup safe.

Row-by-row assessment:
K1: The replacement composition is correct for the old call sites with ignored results: existing-target guard, cursor hit-test, fullscreen/decorations check, and beginDragTarget with the documented defaults. The candidate bool is not an equivalent SDispatchResult, but that is immaterial while every caller ignores it. The proportional hotspot change is supported by MAPDRAGHOTSPOT and is RD, including fullscreen as section 2 and the summary acknowledge. The floating movement equivalence follows from the stated hotspot algebra. Focusing the bar window does not determine the hit-test result; the row correctly retains cursor selection. Strict equivalence remains conditional on the documented threshold/release differences and owner acceptance.
K2: The resize candidate and ignored return are appropriate. Selecting the cursor window rather than the addressed/focused window is inherited behavior, not a new port regression. RD is defensible as an existing observable hazard requiring acceptance if it is being reconsidered; it should not be presented as a newly introduced API difference. Switching to the addressed layoutTarget would require an explicit behavior decision. The backend resizing call is a real implementation change, but the supplied backend implementation is insufficient to establish a new client-visible effect; do not assert one from its name alone.
K3: The guarded endDragTarget replacement is correct, and ignoring bool preserves these call sites. Ending any active drag is inherited behavior and DI as a replacement comparison. This does not justify using the same unconditional behavior for the new unload ownership requirement. Grouping, decoration dispatch, focus and geometry effects remain relevant and are acknowledged, subject to the omitted state-reset issue above.
K4: Enabling floating on the focused window matches the documented legacy translation, provided the stated activewindow selector equivalence holds. ActionResult is the right result type. The floatWindow diff supports the direct replacement; the safer internally guarded end call does not require matching old host internals.
K5: The parser, GOAL size, explicit absolute resize, and invalid-size guard reproduce the supplied translator. Preserve its focused-window selection and no-window guard as well; W must not silently become the bar's window. The document already calls for reproducing selection and the guard. DI is appropriate.
K6: Toggle pin on the focused window is the supplied legacy mapping, with ActionResult. The state-storage/scheduling changes alone do not demonstrate a contract difference. DI is reasonable, with the proposed workspace-during-touch-drag test.
K7: Parsing against GOAL position and calling move(POS, false, W) matches the translator. A direct Vector2D is equivalent here only if it preserves the explicit integer casts in the actual call site; retaining fractional COORDS would change placement. The row's integer qualification is important. DI is otherwise supported.
K8: Disabling floating is the correct settiled mapping and has the same result considerations as K4. DI is appropriate.
K9: The deterministic guarded end matches the documented outside-bind state of -1; the leading character was indeed removed by mouseDispatcher rather than serving as a direct release flag. If reentrant execution under m_passPressed == 1 is possible, equivalence fails, but the supplied material identifies no such path. That remains a hypothesis, not an established blocker. The DI mapping is conditional on the stated outside-bind execution premise.
K10: The supplied translator explicitly maps argument 1 to MAXIMIZED, everything else here to FULLSCREEN, and supplies true for toggle. The proposed calls and ActionResult are correct; DI is supported.
K11: The proposed string overload and silent=true have the documented shape. Workspace-name resolution and readiness remain semantic matters that a return-type probe cannot establish. The planned special:minimized/no-follow test addresses the actual contract. Changed fallback focus is RD, not BC under the owner's stated requirements. Pointer-constraint suspension is also acknowledged; its observable consequences are not established by the excerpt. No failure of the required workspace name or silent movement has been demonstrated.
K12: Direct spawn(cmd) preserves the supplied wrapper's execution operation, and optional<uint64_t> is correct. The wrapper converted failure into SDispatchResult, but the old callers ignored it, so discarding spawn's result is equivalent at these call sites. DI is supported.
K13: Direct typed dispatch is appropriate for this fixed known operation set, but its error account needs the correction in the finding. Choosing to log previously discarded errors is a separate diagnostic-policy change, not something demanded by the replacement API.

Section 2 is broadly accurate. exclusiveDeviceGrab was already a parameter, and retaining false is the appropriate equivalence choice. Nothing supplied requires enabling it for Kwinish or using it as an ownership marker. Its accessor does not identify who started a drag. The new dragEnd bool means that an initial target existed, not that a particular plugin session was ended or that execution reached the final geometry/focus path: the diff has multiple early returns of true. Ignoring it is valid for K1–K3/K9. The ended scope guard is created only after the no-target return, so an empty end does not emit ended. The host's DRAG_WAS_ACTIVE use is consistent with its old ensureMouseBindState role in the excerpts; there is no demonstrated additional Kwinish requirement caused merely by the return-type change.

For Q4, ordinary weak-pointer expiration protects against confusing a destroyed object with a newly allocated object at the same address; the supplied WP implementation itself is not shown. Regardless, the decisive bug uses the same live target and needs no allocator assumption. A rejected begin with a null resulting target is not a missed active plugin drag. However, recording after a K1/K2 helper that returned early because another drag already existed could adopt that drag; the text must distinguish an actual accepted begin from a helper invocation. Recording must also cover every accepted rearm/unsnap restart and luaGrab start. Under that premise, the material does not independently demonstrate an accepted plugin drag that target recording necessarily misses. Calling end while the module is still mapped can synchronously reenter it; whether callbacks can run after unload requires the separate lifecycle proof, not an ended-listener grep.

Probe K genuinely checks compilability, several exact manager/controller member signatures, return types, enum values, callable old-member absence, and the candidate composition. Its negative cases and mutation results are meaningful within that scope. They do not prove runtime behavior, default argument values, successful drag acquisition, ownership, workspace naming, or unload quiescence. Most of those limits are already honestly documented. The supplied P6 closure does not warrant reopening the separately approved logging step.
